- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; model tends to be too optimistic.
- Underestimate during sharp upward trends; model fails to capture momentum or policy-driven spikes.
- Overshoot after sudden price spikes; model reacts too quickly, then corrects too aggressively.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model often forecasts a “return to average” too early, missing sustained upward trends.
- Lag in recognizing true breakout points; model delays confirmation of major price increases.
- Overfit to recent history; model overweights recent high values, underweights low values in the 30-day window.
- Underestimate volatility in the final 5–10 days; model flattens out too early, missing late-stage momentum.
- Forecast bias toward higher values in the last 10–15 days; model tends to overpredict upward continuation.
